title: How to Stir Up a Cold Heart
summary: God is not mocked: we reap what we sow. Sow into the word, fellowship, hospitality and prayer, and he will stir your affection for Jesus.
exhortation: My question this morning is this: how can we as Christians stir up a cold heart with affection and love for Jesus? I've been young, and now I'm kind of old. There have been times I couldn't wait to wake up and get into the word, and times when for some reason my heart resists it or fades. When I was young, I think I assumed it would get easier as I matured. That hasn't been the case. And yet God has met me through it all.

I start with this verse because one of the things I love most about Scripture is that it works, better than we think. God sees the intentions of our hearts. There are scriptures about money that say if you give, God will bless you, and that is absolutely true. But God sees the heart. Ananias and Sapphira held some back, gave with the wrong intentions, and reaped what they sowed. The same is true of our devotion. Are you sowing?
So how do we sow? Acts 2:42 gives a simple breakdown: "And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers."

The apostles' teaching: don't neglect the word of God. Whether you feel it or not, get up and read your Bible. I read from Genesis to Revelation, and when I reach the end I start over. Lately I've added a proverb a day, and it has been like a key that unlocks the rest of Scripture.

The fellowship: who are you spending time with? Are you going to church and fellowshipping with believers, or is most of your time spent feeding yourself on the world, online or on your phone? Either way, you are sowing.

The breaking of bread: are you inviting people into your home and breaking bread with people who love Jesus? It isn't hard. It's actually a blast. Have a family or a couple over who are passionate for Jesus, have a great conversation, and feel your heart stirred with affection for him.

And prayer. I love prayer, so why do I neglect it so much? I think because it takes time and it's relational. But when we pour out our hearts to God and have a real conversation with him, nothing stirs our affection like it. So let's not complain that it's so hard. Let's look at our lives and ask, "Am I sowing?" If you sow, God will bless you by stirring up your affection for him. He hears, and he is quick to come to us.
prayer: Lord, our prayer is that you would stir up our affections. Put your glory, a desire to obey your commands and a love for your word and your ways in our inner man, and let that be paramount in our lives.

I pray for everyone who doesn't have those feelings right now. Give them the faith to obey: to read your word this morning, to take time to pray, and to seek out godly fellowship with people who will stir up their hearts. Let us reflect those early Christians in Acts, filled with the Spirit and newly transformed to love Jesus, who immediately turned to the word, prayer and fellowship. Let that stir our hearts this morning as well.
